Author: Shekhar Kumar Yadav

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Vivek Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Abhishek Kumar Jaiswal,G.A.,Sumant Krishna Singh
Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and learned counsel for the informant as well as perused the material available on record.

2. By means of this application, the applicant- Savej is seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.192 of 2024, under Sections 354-C, 506, 384, 376 IPC, Section 67 of IT Act, Police Station- Ramala, District- Baghpat.

3. As per prosecution story, marriage of the informant had performed with the Mustafa about 10 years ago, informant went at her parental house at village Asara and one day she was taking bath in her bathroom and in the meantime, the applicant make her video and after sometime he made a phone call and informed that he has her video and made pressure to make physical relation with Naeem vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112658588/
1 him and has threatened to viral the video.

It is alleged that the applicant committed rape upon her and in the month of November, 2023 he took Rs.10000/- from her and on 22-12-2023 he again demanded Rs.45,000/- and on 18-06- 2024 he again committed rape upon her and also viral her video.
4. Contention as raised at the Bar by learned counsel for the applicant is that applicant-accused is quite innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The applicant has never committed any offence as alleged in the impugned FIR.
The applicant has neither made any video of the victim nor he has viral as well as nor demanded any money from her.
The incident is alleged to have occurred in November, 2023 whereas the impugned FIR has been lodged on 24.7.2024 for which no explanation of delay has been mentioned.
There is no eye witness of the alleged incident.
Further contention is that there is material contradiction in the statement under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
As per medical report, no mark of any external and internal injury seen all over the body of the victim. Prima facie no offence is made out against the applicant.
5. Several other submissions in order to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against the applicant have also been placed forth before the Court.
The circumstances which, according to the counsel, led to the false implication of the accused have also been touched upon at length.
It has been assured on behalf of the applicant that he is ready to cooperate with the process of law and shall faithfully make himself available before the court whenever required.
Lastly, it is argued that the applicant is languishing in jail since 25.7.2024 having no previous criminal history.

6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the prayer for bail to the applicant by contending that the act committed by the accused-applicant as mentioned in the F.I.R. is a heinous offence.
There is no reason to falsely implicate the applicant.
Innocence of the applicant cannot be ad-judged at pre-trial stage, hence, the bail application of the applicant is liable to be rejected.

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as submission advanced by learned counsel for the parties, nature of allegations, role assigned to the applicant, gravity of offence and all attending facts and circumstances of case, particularly, seeing the fact that the applicant has made video of the victim while she was taking bath and the applicant has committed rape several times and demanded money from the victim as well as send the video to her husband, this Court is of the opinion that it is not a fit case for bail.
8. Accordingly, the bail application is rejected.

Order Date :- 12.11.2024 Krishna*
